A focused TextInput is the terminal's own cursor, shaped by DECSCUSR; the pointer takes the hovered widget's shape by OSC 22 (rich-control-codes-xh4n.sk3) (#561)

* A focused TextInput is the terminal's own cursor, shaped by DECSCUSR; the pointer takes the hovered widget's shape by OSC 22 (rich-control-codes-xh4n.sk3)

The painter hid the hardware cursor for the whole take, so DECSCUSR alone
showed nothing. A frame now names the cell where the terminal's cursor
stands (Style.caret); SurfaceRenderer shows it there in that shape after
each paint, hides it while painting, homes from the caret's row, and gives
the default shape back on hand-back. TextInput marks its caret instead of
drawing a blinking one wherever the painter shows the cursor
(RenderOptions.caret), so an IME and a screen reader follow the editing
point. A logical-order terminal reorders glyphs off their frame columns, so
there the drawn caret stays.

OSC 22 adopted: Console.setPointerShape, App.pointerShape, and
WidgetBase/TextInput.pointerShape set from hover. OSC 133 rejected; the
reason is on the ticket.

* Review fixes: caret column skips control segments, shape written on change, pointer shape survives suspend (rich-control-codes-xh4n.sk3)
